items.title: Matchday details and safer participation controls
items.summary: Liga do Povo replaced the older match detail treatment with an interactive matchday board and made participation controls reflect the actual game state.
details: The match page now presents time, place, availability, gear, and community-listing context through one responsive matchday surface.
Join, leave, waitlist, directions, and organiser-access actions now change according to listing type, public-location availability, and whether a game is scheduled, completed, or cancelled.
The smoke suite checks the board on mobile, verifies its interactive state, and confirms that the rendered scene has a usable visual signal.

items.title: Recurring game discovery and directory trust
items.summary: The pickup directory was expanded around recurring community games, clearer participation rules, and more reliable regional discovery.
details: The directory gained additional field and recurring-series coverage, including Dallas and North Jersey, while keeping area preference explicit.
Community listings now distinguish Liga attendance, external registration, informational listings, known capacity, and public-location access instead of treating every game as the same kind of RSVP.
Recurring schedule, area preference, participation safety, and production persistence are covered by dedicated checks and database migrations.

items.title: Stable recurring-game links during outages
items.summary: Recurring game identifiers were made deterministic so a known game keeps the same link when the shared backend is unavailable.
details: Offline materialisation now derives the same occurrence identifier as the seeded and shared-data paths.
That small invariant prevents bookmarked or shared game routes from changing simply because the application has fallen back to local data.
The change supports a broader design goal: discovery should degrade gracefully without breaking the address of an existing community game.

items.title: Runtime checks distinguish failures from unavailable providers
items.summary: Au Jour Le Jour hardened its Janitor runtime checks so provider outages, quota limits, and missing connections are not reported as application defects unless live-provider availability is required.
details: The check classifies temporary provider and network conditions separately from authentication and application failures.
Optional live-provider tests can be skipped with a precise reason; strict runs remain available through an explicit runtime-required setting.
Advisor requests and provider-connectivity checks now follow the same failure policy, making automated verification less noisy without hiding real defects.

items.title: Readable, recoverable household-ledger backups
items.summary: Au Jour Le Jour added a portable HTML backup that can be read without the application while retaining the original importable data.
details: The export includes recurring bills, monthly items, reserved buckets, payment-derived totals, status counts, and the covered period in a self-contained document.
The raw JSON remains embedded and downloadable, so the readable copy is also a recovery path rather than a dead-end report.
Backup state is updated consistently for JSON and readable exports, and Janitor checks verify that the feature is wired in both builds.
